title: Job, Chapter 33 (Leningrad Codex)
source: Leningrad Codex folios (Internet Archive, WSRP photographs) + tanach.us LC folio index + UXLC Hebrew + KJV
description: Job 33 on folios 406r, 406v of the Leningrad Codex (1008 AD), the oldest complete Hebrew Bible. Hebrew from the UXLC transcription of this manuscript; English KJV.
introduction:
Job chapter 33 from the Leningrad Codex (Codex Leningradensis, National Library of Russia, Firkovich EBP. I B 19a), copied in Cairo by Samuel ben Jacob and dated 1008/1009 AD, the oldest complete manuscript of the Hebrew Bible and the base text of the Biblia Hebraica editions. This chapter stands on folios 406r, 406v.

This entry meets the strict three-criteria standard of the Theosis Library:

  1. Manuscript scan: the specific folio side(s) carrying each section's verses, from the full-colour West Semitic Research Project photographs of the codex as redistributed on Internet Archive (item Leningrad_Codex_Color_Images, marked Creative Commons Public Domain Mark 1.0). Folio-to-verse ranges come from the tanach.us LC folio index, which was derived from the West Semitic Research Project's published index; each section links only to the page(s) whose recorded verse range contains its verses.
  2. Original text: the verbatim Hebrew of this manuscript in the Unicode/XML Leningrad Codex (UXLC 2.5 build 27.6, tanach.us), a transcription of Firkovich B 19a with vowels and cantillation, released without restriction on the biblical text.
  3. English translation: the King James Version (1611, public domain), retrieved verbatim from bolls.life (KJV text, Strong's numbers stripped).
translator_notes: Ketiv/Qere: where the scribe wrote one form (ketiv) but the Masoretes read another (qere), the consonantal ketiv is given first and the vocalised qere follows in square brackets. פ and ס mark the open and closed paragraph breaks visible as gaps in the manuscript columns.

translation.original_text: <sup>1</sup>וְֽאוּלָ֗ם שְׁמַֽע־נָ֣א אִיּ֣וֹב מִלָּ֑י וְֽכָל־דְּבָרַ֥י הַאֲזִֽינָה׃ <sup>2</sup>הִנֵּה־נָ֭א פָּתַ֣חְתִּי פִ֑י דִּבְּרָ֖ה לְשׁוֹנִ֣י בְחִכִּֽי׃ <sup>3</sup>יֹֽשֶׁר־לִבִּ֥י אֲמָרָ֑י וְדַ֥עַת שְׂ֝פָתַ֗י בָּר֥וּר מִלֵּֽלוּ׃ <sup>4</sup>רֽוּחַ־אֵ֥ל עָשָׂ֑תְנִי וְנִשְׁמַ֖ת שַׁדַּ֣י תְּחַיֵּֽנִי׃ <sup>5</sup>אִם־תּוּכַ֥ל הֲשִׁיבֵ֑נִי עֶרְכָ֥ה לְ֝פָנַ֗י הִתְיַצָּֽבָה׃ <sup>6</sup>הֵן־אֲנִ֣י כְפִ֣יךָ לָאֵ֑ל מֵ֝חֹ֗מֶר קֹרַ֥צְתִּי גַם־אָֽנִי׃ <sup>7</sup>הִנֵּ֣ה אֵ֭מָתִי לֹ֣א תְבַעֲתֶ֑ךָּ וְ֝אַכְפִּ֗י עָלֶ֥יךָ לֹא־יִכְבָּֽד׃ <sup>8</sup>אַ֭ךְ אָמַ֣רְתָּ בְאָזְנָ֑י וְק֖וֹל מִלִּ֣ין אֶשְׁמָֽע׃
translation.text: <sup>1</sup>Wherefore, Job, I pray thee, hear my speeches, and hearken to all my words. <sup>2</sup>Behold, now I have opened my mouth, my tongue hath spoken in my mouth. <sup>3</sup>My words shall be of the uprightness of my heart: and my lips shall utter knowledge clearly. <sup>4</sup>The Spirit of God hath made me, and the breath of the Almighty hath given me life. <sup>5</sup>If thou canst answer me, set thy words in order before me, stand up. <sup>6</sup>Behold, I am according to thy wish in God's stead: I also am formed out of the clay. <sup>7</sup>Behold, my terror shall not make thee afraid, neither shall my hand be heavy upon thee. <sup>8</sup>Surely thou hast spoken in mine hearing, and I have heard the voice of thy words, saying,

translation.original_text: <sup>9</sup>זַ֥ךְ אֲנִ֗י בְּֽלִ֫י פָ֥שַׁע חַ֥ף אָנֹכִ֑י וְלֹ֖א עָוֺ֣ן לִֽי׃ <sup>10</sup>הֵ֣ן תְּ֭נוּאוֹת עָלַ֣י יִמְצָ֑א יַחְשְׁבֵ֖נִי לְאוֹיֵ֣ב לֽוֹ׃ <sup>11</sup>יָשֵׂ֣ם בַּסַּ֣ד רַגְלָ֑י יִ֝שְׁמֹ֗ר כָּל־אָרְחֹתָֽי׃ <sup>12</sup>הֶן־זֹ֣את לֹא־צָדַ֣קְתָּ אֶעֱנֶ֑ךָּ כִּֽי־יִרְבֶּ֥ה אֱ֝ל֗וֹהַ מֵאֱנֽוֹשׁ׃ <sup>13</sup>מַ֭דּוּעַ אֵלָ֣יו רִיב֑וֹתָ כִּ֥י כָל־דְּ֝בָרָ֗יו לֹ֣א יַעֲנֶֽה׃ <sup>14</sup>כִּֽי־בְאַחַ֥ת יְדַבֶּר־אֵ֑ל וּ֝בִשְׁתַּ֗יִם לֹ֣א יְשׁוּרֶֽנָּה׃ <sup>15</sup>בַּחֲל֤וֹם ׀ חֶזְי֬וֹן לַ֗יְלָה בִּנְפֹ֣ל תַּ֭רְדֵּמָה עַל־אֲנָשִׁ֑ים בִּ֝תְנוּמ֗וֹת עֲלֵ֣י מִשְׁכָּֽב׃ <sup>16</sup>אָ֣ז יִ֭גְלֶה אֹ֣זֶן אֲנָשִׁ֑ים וּבְמֹ֖סָרָ֣ם יַחְתֹּֽם׃
translation.text: <sup>9</sup>I am clean without transgression, I am innocent; neither is there iniquity in me. <sup>10</sup>Behold, he findeth occasions against me, he counteth me for his enemy, <sup>11</sup>He putteth my feet in the stocks, he marketh all my paths. <sup>12</sup>Behold, in this thou art not just: I will answer thee, that God is greater than man. <sup>13</sup>Why dost thou strive against him? for he giveth not account of any of his matters. <sup>14</sup>For God speaketh once, yea twice, yet man perceiveth it not. <sup>15</sup>In a dream, in a vision of the night, when deep sleep falleth upon men, in slumberings upon the bed; <sup>16</sup>Then he openeth the ears of men, and sealeth their instruction,

translation.original_text: <sup>17</sup>לְ֭הָסִיר אָדָ֣ם מַעֲשֶׂ֑ה וְגֵוָ֖ה מִגֶּ֣בֶר יְכַסֶּֽה׃ <sup>18</sup>יַחְשֹׂ֣ךְ נַ֭פְשׁוֹ מִנִּי־שָׁ֑חַת וְ֝חַיָּת֗וֹ מֵעֲבֹ֥ר בַּשָּֽׁלַח׃ <sup>19</sup>וְהוּכַ֣ח בְּ֭מַכְאוֹב עַל־מִשְׁכָּב֑וֹ וריב [וְר֖וֹב] עֲצָמָ֣יו אֵתָֽן׃ <sup>20</sup>וְזִֽהֲמַ֣תּוּ חַיָּת֣וֹ לָ֑חֶם וְ֝נַפְשׁ֗וֹ מַאֲכַ֥ל תַּאֲוָֽה׃ <sup>21</sup>יִ֣כֶל בְּשָׂר֣וֹ מֵרֹ֑אִי ושפי [וְשֻׁפּ֥וּ] עַ֝צְמוֹתָ֗יו לֹ֣א רֻאּֽוּ׃ <sup>22</sup>וַתִּקְרַ֣ב לַשַּׁ֣חַת נַפְשׁ֑וֹ וְ֝חַיָּת֗וֹ לַֽמְמִתִֽים׃ <sup>23</sup>אִם־יֵ֤שׁ עָלָ֨יו ׀ מַלְאָ֗ךְ מֵלִ֗יץ אֶחָ֥ד מִנִּי־אָ֑לֶף לְהַגִּ֖יד לְאָדָ֣ם יָשְׁרֽוֹ׃ <sup>24</sup>וַיְחֻנֶּ֗נּוּ וַיֹּ֗אמֶר פְּ֭דָעֵהוּ מֵרֶ֥דֶת שָׁ֗חַת מָצָ֥אתִי כֹֽפֶר׃
translation.text: <sup>17</sup>That he may withdraw man from his purpose, and hide pride from man. <sup>18</sup>He keepeth back his soul from the pit, and his life from perishing by the sword. <sup>19</sup>He is chastened also with pain upon his bed, and the multitude of his bones with strong pain: <sup>20</sup>So that his life abhorreth bread, and his soul dainty meat. <sup>21</sup>His flesh is consumed away, that it cannot be seen; and his bones that were not seen stick out. <sup>22</sup>Yea, his soul draweth near unto the grave, and his life to the destroyers. <sup>23</sup>If there be a messenger with him, an interpreter, one among a thousand, to shew unto man his uprightness: <sup>24</sup>Then he is gracious unto him, and saith, Deliver him from going down to the pit: I have found a ransom.

translation.original_text: <sup>25</sup>רֻֽטֲפַ֣שׁ בְּשָׂר֣וֹ מִנֹּ֑עַר יָ֝שׁ֗וּב לִימֵ֥י עֲלוּמָֽיו׃ <sup>26</sup>יֶעְתַּ֤ר אֶל־אֱל֨וֹהַּ ׀ וַיִּרְצֵ֗הוּ וַיַּ֣רְא פָּ֭נָיו בִּתְרוּעָ֑ה וַיָּ֥שֶׁב לֶ֝אֱנ֗וֹשׁ צִדְקָתֽוֹ׃ <sup>27</sup>יָשֹׁ֤ר ׀ עַל־אֲנָשִׁ֗ים וַיֹּ֗אמֶר חָ֭טָאתִי וְיָשָׁ֥ר הֶעֱוֵ֗יתִי וְלֹא־שָׁ֥וָה לִֽי׃ <sup>28</sup>פָּדָ֣ה נפשי [נַ֭פְשׁוֹ] מֵעֲבֹ֣ר בַּשָּׁ֑חַת וחיתי [וְ֝חַיָּתוֹ] בָּא֥וֹר תִּרְאֶֽה׃ <sup>29</sup>הֶן־כָּל־אֵ֭לֶּה יִפְעַל־אֵ֑ל פַּעֲמַ֖יִם שָׁל֣וֹשׁ עִם־גָּֽבֶר׃ <sup>30</sup>לְהָשִׁ֣יב נַ֭פְשׁוֹ מִנִּי־שָׁ֑חַת לֵ֝א֗וֹר בְּא֣וֹר הַֽחַיִּים׃ <sup>31</sup>הַקְשֵׁ֖ב אִיּ֥וֹב שְֽׁמַֽע־לִ֑י הַ֝חֲרֵ֗שׁ וְאָנֹכִ֥י אֲדַבֵּֽר׃ <sup>32</sup>אִם־יֵשׁ־מִלִּ֥ין הֲשִׁיבֵ֑נִי דַּ֝בֵּ֗ר כִּֽי־חָפַ֥צְתִּי צַדְּקֶֽךָּ׃ <sup>33</sup>אִם־אַ֭יִן אַתָּ֥ה שְֽׁמַֽע־לִ֑י הַ֝חֲרֵ֗שׁ וַאֲאַלֶּפְךָ֥ חָכְמָֽה׃ ס
translation.text: <sup>25</sup>His flesh shall be fresher than a child's: he shall return to the days of his youth: <sup>26</sup>He shall pray unto God, and he will be favourable unto him: and he shall see his face with joy: for he will render unto man his righteousness. <sup>27</sup>He looketh upon men, and if any say, I have sinned, and perverted that which was right, and it profited me not; <sup>28</sup>He will deliver his soul from going into the pit, and his life shall see the light. <sup>29</sup>Lo, all these things worketh God oftentimes with man, <sup>30</sup>To bring back his soul from the pit, to be enlightened with the light of the living. <sup>31</sup>Mark well, O Job, hearken unto me: hold thy peace, and I will speak. <sup>32</sup>If thou hast any thing to say, answer me: speak, for I desire to justify thee. <sup>33</sup>If not, hearken unto me: hold thy peace, and I shall teach thee wisdom.
